clue.text: Band's record — piano included in rearranged prelude

definitions.note: the definition reads as 'band is', naming a rock group

indicators.note: one group of letters is placed inside another, as something included sits within it
the letters of prelude are put into a new order

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A group's new release adds a piano part to a reworked opening piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band's' reads as 'band is', so the definition is the group itself; 'rearranged' scrambles the seven letters and 'included in' splits them after the first two.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running British hard-rock group famous for Smoke on the Water.

indicators.note: drinking in, so one piece takes another inside it
most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to advocate is to recommend or urge

explanation.surface: Someone suggests drinking a sweet after-dinner spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts ADVOCATE to ADVOCAT, and 'imbibing' puts A inside it before the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch egg-and-brandy drink, the base of the snowball cocktail.

parts.note: the cream is the best part of anything

explanation.surface: A runner-up in a contest of funny performers.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling someone 'a scream' means they are hilarious, so a comic can be one.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a very funny person is called a riot or a hoot, the same idea.

indicators.note: confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A crew staffed a vessel out on the ocean as a team.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting jointly or side by side, like a two-seater bicycle.

definitions.meaning: a book by Sir Walter Scott about a Highland outlaw
a whisky drink akin to a Manhattan, named after the same outlaw

explanation.surface: A newfangled mixed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish outlaw's name titles both a Walter Scott book and a Scotch-based mixed drink.

clue.text: Frantic friar employing force against very loud undesirables

indicators.note: set beside, so one piece is placed next to the other
using, so one piece holds another inside it
wild and agitated, so the letters of friar are scrambled

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force
FF is fortissimo in music

explanation.surface: A frenzied monk uses violence while shouting at disreputable people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frantic' scrambles the monk's five letters, 'employing' tucks the force letter among them, and 'against' sets the musical loudness mark alongside at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissive term for disreputable, rowdy people of low standing.

indicators.note: going without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Chancellor's annual financial statement with no content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Budget' suggests the British Chancellor's annual speech, but here it is a verb meaning to allot sparingly.
explanation.definitionFit: To budget something is to allocate it in limited portions, as with wartime food allowances.

clue.text: Jolly place to eat, no car required

definitions.note: in British slang, jolly is an adverb as in 'jolly good'

indicators.note: without, so the named letters are dropped

parts.note: a carvery is a restaurant serving roast meats carved to order

explanation.surface: A cheerful restaurant where you need not drive.
explanation.walkthrough: A carvery is a British restaurant serving carved roasts; 'Jolly' as in 'jolly good' is British slang for extremely.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are intensifying adverbs meaning extremely, as in 'jolly well' or 'most well'.

definitions.meaning: a close is a conclusion, as of a day
a finish is a final stage or conclusion

explanation.surface: A photo finish, a near-run thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name the final point or conclusion of something.

indicators.note: open to attack and breakable, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Shore up a weak fortress quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To make firmer or more solid, as in shoring up a position.

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: a robe is a long gown

explanation.surface: Inspect the bodice of a lovely dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to investigate or look into something closely.

parts.note: airy means casual or offhand in manner
a hob is a hobgoblin, an example of a sprite

explanation.surface: A casual attitude to a cooker top, seemingly impractical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hob' looks like a cooker top, but it is an old word for a hobgoblin or elf.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes ideas that are fanciful and impractical, not grounded.

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the aitch from words

parts.note: safe means unhurt; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class East Londoners, famously drop their H sounds, so the H vanishes from UNHARMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Without weapons, a person is defenceless and exposed to attack.

indicators.note: in the end, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: earned means gained through work

explanation.surface: Peace was craved and finally achieved.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to have pined or wished deeply for something.

clue.text: Send in lady to reform theme park

more means again, as in 'once more'
standards are banners or flags

indicators.note: moving about, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: A modern number performed by a leading pair of dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean modern or current, abreast of the latest.

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king
ambling is strolling at an easy pace

clue.text: A horse taken initially inside to drink

the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes T from 'taken', and 'inside' puts it within TO to give TTO.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian almond-flavoured liqueur is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Resilient European to remain in charge

parts.note: to last is to endure or remain

explanation.surface: A tough continental official keeps his post.

clue.text: Guitarist, celebrity, coming over after a kiss

indicators.note: one piece follows the others

parts.note: X is the conventional letter for a kiss

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming over turns the word backwards

parts.note: a big name is a celebrity

explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'coming over' means read upwards, so the celebrity word turns round; 'after' puts it behind the article and the kiss.
